title: DR1 lets a user start any task on the hub from the first visit; the frontend greys nine of its eleven rows out as "Cannot start yet" until a country of origin and a commodity have been answered.

finding.frontend: On a notification where only the country of origin has been given, nine of the eleven hub rows carry no link and read "Cannot start yet" — Main reason for importing, Additional commodity details, Animal identification details, Arrival details, Transporter, Roles and addresses, Contact address, Uploaded documents and Check and submit. Only "Where is this consignment coming from?" and "What are you importing?" can be opened. The whole task list is held behind two answers: the country of origin and a commodity selection, the two obligations enforced at continue in src/server/app/bridge/obligation-source.js:31-34. A row is offered only when the first page behind it clears that check (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:103-124); otherwise the row is rendered without a link and its real status is replaced by "Cannot start yet" (:95).
finding.prototype: Every row of DR1's task list is a link on every visit, whatever has been answered. The hub view model gives each of the twelve items a fixed href and one of exactly two statuses, "To do" or "Complete" (app/routes.js:5734-5837), so a user who has just created a notification can go straight to Transport details or Upload documents if that is what they have to hand.
finding.difference: Stop withholding hub rows. Render every task row as a link and let its status describe progress instead of permission, which means dropping the gate consulted in controller.js:120 and the "Cannot start yet" substitution at :95, and letting each page cope with being opened before its neighbours. The frontend's "cannot start" state is not the same thing as a page being unreachable: the questions behind the blocked rows are still asked, because a new notification is walked forward through origin, commodity search, commodity details, reason for import, animal identification and additional details before it ever lands on the hub (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-38), and every row unblocks the moment a commodity exists — the fe-hub capture, taken one answer later, shows all eleven rows startable. What DR1 gives and the frontend does not is the choice of where to start.
finding.falsifiedBy: A frontend hub rendered with neither a country of origin nor a commodity answered in which the Arrival details or Uploaded documents row is a working link.

relatedTo.why: the Check and submit row is blocked by the same mechanism, but its replacement of DR1's always-available Review and submit button is a separate change
the same gate, but that row never unblocks at all, so removing the gate fixes both
